title: Reporting and Persuading
description: Summarise conversations and arguments with reporting verbs followed by an infinitive, an -ing form or a that-clause; report commands and requests; and decide when backshift is unnecessary. Vocabulary: negotiation, persuasion and the media.
objectives: Use reporting verbs with the correct pattern (to-infinitive, -ing, that-clause)
Report commands, requests and advice accurately
Report speech without backshift when the information is still true
Summarise discussions and negotiations using precise reporting verbs

lessons.title: Reporting Verbs + Infinitive
lessons.summary: Kata kerja pelaporan yang diikuti to-infinitive (agree, offer, refuse) dan objek + to-infinitive (advise, warn, remind).
objectives: Use verb + to-infinitive: agree, offer, promise, refuse, threaten, claim
Use verb + object + to-infinitive: advise, warn, remind, persuade, encourage, invite
Choose a reporting verb that summarises the speaker's intention
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Beyond say and tell
At B2 level, instead of repeating every word with *said*, we choose a **reporting verb** that shows the speaker's **intention**: offering, refusing, warning, promising. This makes reports shorter and more precise.

*'I'll carry your bag,' Tom said.* → *Tom **offered to carry** my bag.*

### Pattern A: verb + to-infinitive
| Verb | Direct speech | Report |
| --- | --- | --- |
| agree | "OK, I'll help." | She **agreed to help**. |
| offer | "Shall I drive you home?" | He **offered to drive** me home. |
| promise | "I'll be on time." | They **promised to be** on time. |
| refuse | "I won't sign it!" | She **refused to sign** it. |
| threaten | "Pay, or I'll call the police!" | He **threatened to call** the police. |
| claim | "I'm a qualified pilot." | He **claimed to be** a qualified pilot. |

### Pattern B: verb + object + to-infinitive
| Verb | Direct speech | Report |
| --- | --- | --- |
| advise | "You should rest." | The doctor **advised me to rest**. |
| warn | "Don't swim here!" | He **warned us not to swim** there. |
| remind | "Don't forget to call Mum." | She **reminded me to call** Mum. |
| persuade | (after a long discussion) | I **persuaded him to stay**. |
| encourage | "Go on, apply!" | She **encouraged me to apply**. |
| invite | "Would you like to come?" | They **invited us to come**. |

### Negatives
Put **not** before *to*: *He warned us **not to touch** the wires.* / *She promised **not to tell** anyone.*

### Time and place changes still apply
When the report is later, change pronouns and time words as usual: *"I'll call you tomorrow"* → *She promised to call me **the next day**.*

### Typical mistakes
- ✗ *She suggested me to go* — *suggest* does NOT take object + infinitive (see the next lesson).
- ✗ *He refused helping* — *refuse* takes to-infinitive.
- ✗ *They advised to me to wait* — no *to* before the object.

> **Catatan:** Banyak kata kerja ini mirip dalam bahasa Indonesia (*menawarkan untuk, menolak untuk, berjanji untuk*), jadi polanya mudah: **verb + to + V1**. Untuk *advise, warn, remind, persuade*, objeknya (orang) langsung setelah kata kerja: *menasihati **saya** untuk...* = *advised **me** to...*

lessons.title: Reporting Verbs + -ing
lessons.summary: Kata kerja pelaporan yang diikuti -ing (deny, admit, suggest) dan preposisi + -ing (apologise for, accuse of, insist on).
objectives: Use verb + -ing: admit, deny, suggest, recommend
Use verb + preposition + -ing: apologise for, insist on, object to
Use verb + object + preposition + -ing: accuse of, blame for, congratulate on, thank for
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Pattern C: verb + -ing
| Verb | Direct speech | Report |
| --- | --- | --- |
| admit | "Yes, I took it." | He **admitted taking** it. |
| deny | "I didn't send that email!" | She **denied sending** the email. |
| suggest | "Let's take a taxi." | He **suggested taking** a taxi. |
| recommend | "Try the fish soup." | She **recommended trying** the fish soup. |

*Admit* and *deny* can also use **having + past participle** to stress that the action is in the past: *He denied **having seen** her.* Both forms are correct.

### Pattern D: verb + preposition + -ing
| Verb | Example |
| --- | --- |
| apologise **for** | She **apologised for being** late. |
| insist **on** | He **insisted on paying** for dinner. |
| object **to** | They **objected to working** on Sundays. |
| complain **about** | We **complained about waiting** so long. |

⚠️ *Object to* is followed by **-ing**, because *to* is a preposition here.

### Pattern E: verb + object + preposition + -ing
| Verb | Example |
| --- | --- |
| accuse sb **of** | They **accused him of lying**. |
| blame sb **for** | She **blamed me for losing** the tickets. |
| congratulate sb **on** | We **congratulated her on winning**. |
| thank sb **for** | I **thanked them for helping** me. |
| criticise sb **for** | The report **criticised the council for wasting** money. |

### suggest and recommend: careful!
These verbs **cannot** take *object + to-infinitive*:
- ✗ *She suggested me to take a taxi.*
- ✓ *She suggested **taking** a taxi.*
- ✓ *She suggested **(that) I take / I should take** a taxi.* (that-clause — next lesson)

### Negatives
Put **not** before the -ing form: *He apologised for **not calling**.* / *She admitted **not reading** the contract.*

> **Catatan:** Kesalahan paling umum penutur bahasa Indonesia adalah *suggest someone to do* (karena *menyarankan seseorang untuk*). Dalam bahasa Inggris, **suggest + -ing** atau **suggest that + subjek + verb**. Ingat juga pasangan preposisi: *apologise **for**, insist **on**, accuse **of**, congratulate **on***.

Never say *suggest someone to do*. *Ringkasan: hafalkan preposisinya dan gunakan -ing setelah preposisi.*

lessons.title: Reporting Verbs + That-Clause
lessons.summary: Kata kerja pelaporan dengan that-clause dan kata kerja yang memiliki lebih dari satu pola.
objectives: Use verbs such as explain, complain, point out and insist with that-clauses
Recognise verbs with more than one pattern (admit, deny, promise, suggest, warn)
Avoid errors such as explain me and say me
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Pattern F: verb + that-clause
Many reporting verbs are followed by a **that-clause** (*that* is often omitted in speech):
- *She **explained that** the train had been cancelled.*
- *He **complained that** the room was too cold.*
- *The lawyer **pointed out that** the contract wasn't signed.*
- *They **announced that** the factory would close.*

Usual backshift rules apply when the reporting verb is in the past (*is → was, will → would*).

### Verb + (to + person) + that
Some verbs need **to** before the listener:
| ✓ Correct | ✗ Wrong |
| --- | --- |
| She **explained to me** that... | She explained me that... |
| He **complained to the manager** that... | He complained the manager that... |
| They **said (to us)** that... | They said us that... |

Compare with verbs that take the listener directly: *tell **me**, inform **me**, remind **me**, warn **me**, assure **me** that...*

### Verbs with more than one pattern
| Verb | Pattern 1 | Pattern 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| admit | admitted **taking** it | admitted **that** he had taken it |
| deny | denied **lying** | denied **that** she had lied |
| promise | promised **to call** | promised **that** she would call |
| agree | agreed **to help** | agreed **that** it was a good idea |
| warn | warned us **not to go** | warned us **that** it was dangerous |
| insist | insisted **on paying** | insisted **that** she pay / should pay |
| suggest | suggested **leaving** | suggested **that** we (should) leave |

### suggest / insist / recommend + that
In a that-clause after these verbs, use **should + verb** or the base form (more formal): *The doctor recommended **that** he **(should) rest**.* In informal British English, a past form is also heard: *She suggested I took a taxi.*

### Choosing the pattern
Use a **that-clause** when you report a full idea or fact; use an **infinitive/-ing** when you report an action or intention briefly.

> **Catatan:** Jangan menerjemahkan *menjelaskan kepada saya* menjadi *explain me*; yang benar *explain **to** me*. Begitu pula *say*: *He said to me* atau *He told me*, bukan *He said me*.

mistakes.wrong: The teacher explained us that the exam had been moved.

mistakes.why: Explain needs to before the listener.

mistakes.wrong: He said me that he was busy.

sections.summary: Many reporting verbs take **that + clause**: *explain, complain, point out, announce, admit, deny, agree, promise, warn*. Use **to + listener** after *explain, complain, say*, but no *to* after *tell, inform, assure, remind*. After *suggest/recommend/insist that*, use *(should) + base verb*. *Ringkasan: explain TO me, tell me.*

admit taking / admit that he had taken

lessons.title: Reported Commands and Requests
lessons.summary: Melaporkan perintah dan permintaan dengan tell/ask/order + objek + (not) to.
objectives: Report commands with tell/order/instruct + object + (not) to
Report requests with ask + object + (not) to and ask if/whether...could
Report polite requests such as Would you mind...? and Could you...?
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Commands
Imperatives (*Sit down! Don't move!*) are reported with **verb + object + (not) to + infinitive**.

| Direct speech | Reported |
| --- | --- |
| "Close the door." | He **told me to close** the door. |
| "Don't park here!" | The guard **told us not to park** there. |
| "Stop the car!" (police) | The officer **ordered the driver to stop** the car. |
| "Fill in both pages." | The clerk **instructed us to fill in** both pages. |

Choose the verb according to the situation: *tell* (neutral), *order* (authority), *instruct* (formal procedures), *urge* (strong encouragement), *beg* (emotional request).

### Requests
Requests are reported with **ask + object + (not) to + infinitive**:
| Direct speech | Reported |
| --- | --- |
| "Please sit down." | The nurse **asked me to sit** down. |
| "Could you send me the file?" | She **asked me to send** her the file. |
| "Would you mind turning the music down?" | My neighbour **asked me to turn** the music down. |
| "Please don't tell anyone." | He **asked me not to tell** anyone. |

A request can also be reported as a reported question: *She **asked (me) if I could send** her the file.* (statement word order!)

### Asking for something (noun)
*"Can I have a glass of water?"* → *She **asked for** a glass of water.*

### Common errors
| ✗ Wrong | ✓ Right |
| --- | --- |
| He said me to wait. | He **told** me to wait. / He **asked** me to wait. |
| She told me don't worry. | She told me **not to** worry. |
| They asked to us to leave. | They asked **us** to leave. |
| He told to me to sit. | He told **me** to sit. |

### Pronouns and place words
Remember to change them: *"Leave your bags **here**"* → *He told us to leave our bags **there**.*

> **Catatan:** Untuk melaporkan perintah dan permintaan, bahasa Inggris tidak memakai *that* tetapi **objek + to + V1**: *Dia menyuruh saya menunggu* = *She told me to wait.* Bentuk negatifnya **not to**, bukan *don't*. *Say* tidak bisa langsung diikuti orang + to-infinitive.

lessons.title: Summarising Discussions and Negotiations
lessons.summary: Melaporkan tanpa backshift dan merangkum diskusi atau negosiasi dengan kosakata persuasi.
objectives: Decide when backshift is unnecessary (present reporting verbs, facts still true)
Use vocabulary for negotiation and persuasion (compromise, concession, deadlock)
Summarise a discussion with a range of reporting verbs
lessons.completionCriteria: Complete the speaking task and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Selesaikan tugas berbicara dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Reported speech without backshift
At lower levels you learned to move tenses back (*am → was*). At B2, you should know when this is **not necessary**:

| Situation | Example |
| --- | --- |
| The reporting verb is in the **present** | *Ken **says** he**'s** stuck in traffic.* |
| The information is **still true** | *Maya said she**'s moving** to Medan next year.* (She still plans to.) |
| **General truths / facts** | *Our teacher said that water **boils** at 100°C.* |
| Reporting something said **a moment ago** | *What did he say? — He said he**'s** hungry.* |
| Modals *would, could, should, might, ought to* | They don't change. *"You should rest"* → *She said I **should** rest.* |

Backshift is still correct in these cases (*Maya said she was moving...*), but **not** backshifting shows that the information is still valid. If the situation has **changed or finished**, you must backshift: *He said he **was** single, but now he's married.*

### Summarising a discussion
In meetings and negotiations, we rarely report every word. We **summarise** with precise reporting verbs:

| Function | Reporting verbs |
| --- | --- |
| giving opinions | argue that, claim that, point out that, stress that |
| proposals | propose -ing / that, suggest -ing / that |
| agreement | agree to / that, accept, approve |
| disagreement | reject, refuse to, object to, dispute |
| pressure | urge sb to, insist on / that, warn sb that |

*Ms. Lim **argued that** the budget was too small and **urged** the board **to reconsider**, but the director **refused to change** it.*

### Negotiation and persuasion vocabulary
| Word | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| reach an agreement / a deal | finally agree |
| make a concession | give up something to help agreement |
| (reach a) compromise | a solution where both sides give something |
| deadlock | a situation where no progress is possible |
| counter-offer | an offer made in reply to another offer |
| win sb over | persuade sb to support you |
| convince sb (that) | make sb believe something |

> **Catatan:** Tidak semua kalimat tidak langsung harus 'mundur' tense-nya. Jika informasinya **masih benar** atau kata kerja pelapornya **present** (*says, has said*), tense boleh tetap. Untuk merangkum rapat, pilih kata kerja yang tepat (*argued, proposed, rejected*) daripada mengulang *said* terus-menerus.

examples.en: The manager says the new schedule starts next week.
examples.id: Manajer bilang jadwal baru mulai minggu depan.

examples.en: Our tour guide told us that the temple is over a thousand years old.
examples.id: Pemandu wisata kami mengatakan bahwa candi itu berusia lebih dari seribu tahun.

examples.en: After a week of talks, the union reached a compromise with the company.
examples.id: Setelah seminggu perundingan, serikat pekerja mencapai kompromi dengan perusahaan.

examples.en: The supplier rejected our first offer, so we made a counter-offer.
examples.id: Pemasok menolak tawaran pertama kami, jadi kami mengajukan tawaran balik.

vocabulary.example: Both sides had to compromise.
The company made several concessions.
The talks ended in deadlock.
She convinced me that the plan would work.
His honesty won the audience over.
He argued that the tax was unfair.

grammar.example: She says she needs more time.
grammar.note: No backshift with present reporting verbs.

grammar.example: He said the shop opens at nine.
grammar.note: Optional backshift for facts that are still true.

grammar.example: She stressed that safety came first.

mistakes.wrong: He said me that the talks were in deadlock.
mistakes.right: He told me that the talks were in deadlock.
mistakes.why: Use tell + person, or say (to + person).
The collocation is reach (or come to) a compromise.

mistakes.wrong: Last year he said he is single, but now he's married.
mistakes.right: Last year he said he was single, but now he's married.
mistakes.why: If the situation has changed and is no longer true, you must backshift.

sections.summary: Backshift is **optional** when the reporting verb is present, when the information is still true, or for general facts; modals like *would/could/should/might* never change. Summarise discussions with precise verbs (*argue, propose, reject, urge, insist*) and negotiation vocabulary (*reach a compromise, make a concession, deadlock, counter-offer*). *Ringkasan: masih benar? Tense boleh tetap.*

reviewCards.back: Present reporting verb → keep the tense

questions.prompt: Ken is on the phone right now. He says, "I'm stuck in traffic." Report what he says.
questions.instructions: Hint: the reporting verb is in the present tense.
questions.text: Ken says he ___ stuck in traffic.
questions.explanation: With a present reporting verb (*says*), we don't backshift: **Ken says he is stuck in traffic.**

questions.prompt: Yesterday a scientist said, "Water boils at 100°C at sea level." Which report is correct?
options: She said that water boils at 100°C at sea level.
She said that water had boiled at 100°C at sea level.
She says that water boiled at 100°C at sea level yesterday.
She said that water will have boiled at 100°C at sea level.
questions.explanation: A general scientific fact is still true, so the present simple is natural: **She said that water boils at 100°C.** The past perfect would wrongly suggest a single past event.

questions.prompt: Match each negotiation term with its meaning.

pairs.right: a solution in which both sides give up something
something you give up to help reach an agreement
a situation in which no progress is possible
an offer made in reply to another offer

questions.explanation: These words are typical of business meetings and news reports about negotiations.

questions.prompt: Think of a recent discussion (a family decision, a meeting or a debate in class). Summarise it in about one minute using at least four different reporting verbs and one negotiation term.
questions.sampleAnswer: Last weekend my family discussed where to go on holiday. My brother argued that the beach was the best option because it's cheap. My mother pointed out that it is very hot in July and suggested going to the mountains instead. My father refused to drive more than five hours, and my sister insisted on staying somewhere with Wi-Fi. In the end, we reached a compromise: we're going to a lake that's only three hours away.
questions.explanation: A strong summary uses varied reporting verbs with the correct patterns and avoids repeating *said*.

questions.prompt: An hour ago, Maya told you: "I'm moving to Medan next year." Her plan hasn't changed. Select the TWO correct reports.
options: Maya said she's moving to Medan next year.
Maya said she was moving to Medan next year.
Maya said she is moving to Medan last year.
Maya told she was moving to Medan next year.
Maya said me she was moving to Medan next year.
questions.explanation: Because the plan is still true, both the present (**she's moving**) and the backshifted form (**she was moving**) are correct. *Last year* is illogical; *told* needs an object; *said me* is wrong.

questions.prompt: Complete with ONE word.
questions.text: After hours of discussion, the two sides reached a ___: the union accepted a smaller pay rise, and the company agreed to shorter working hours.
answers: compromise
deal
questions.explanation: Both sides gave up something → **a compromise** (kompromi). *Reach a compromise* is a strong collocation.

questions.prompt: Put the fragments in order to make a summary of a meeting.
fragments: During the meeting, Ms. Lim argued
that the budget was too small
but the director refused to change it.
questions.explanation: **argue that** + clause, **urge + object + to-infinitive**, **refuse + to-infinitive**: three patterns in one summary.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: "I didn't break the vase!" said Leo. Which report is correct?
options: Leo denied breaking the vase.
Leo refused breaking the vase.
Leo denied to break the vase.
Leo admitted breaking the vase.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Saying you didn't do something = **deny + -ing**. *Admit* has the opposite meaning, and *refuse* means 'say you won't do something'.

unitTestQuestions.sentence: "I'll call you as soon as I land," Mum said to me.
answers: Mum promised to call me as soon as she landed.
Mum promised to call me as soon as she lands.
Mum promised that she would call me as soon as she landed.
Mum promised me that she would call me as soon as she landed.
Mum promised she would call me as soon as she landed.
Mum promised me she would call me as soon as she landed.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: **promise + to-infinitive** (or *promise that + would*): *Mum promised to call me as soon as she landed.*

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Complete the text with forms from the bank.
unitTestQuestions.text: The salesman persuaded me ___ the extended warranty, but later I regretted ___ it, so I asked the shop ___ me a refund.
answers: to buy
buying
to give
unitTestQuestions.explanation: **persuade + object + to-infinitive**; **regret + -ing** (for a past action you are sorry about); **ask + object + to-infinitive**.
*Tell* needs a person as object: **She told us that...** (or *She said that...*).

unitTestQuestions.text: At half-time, the coach ___ us not to give up.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: **urge + object + (not) to-infinitive**. *Suggest* and *say* cannot be followed by *us not to...*

unitTestQuestions.source: Ibu mengingatkan saya untuk membawa payung.
answers: My mother reminded me to bring an umbrella.
My mother reminded me to take an umbrella.
Mum reminded me to bring an umbrella.
Mum reminded me to take an umbrella.
Mom reminded me to bring an umbrella.
Mom reminded me to take an umbrella.
My mum reminded me to bring an umbrella.
My mum reminded me to take an umbrella.
My mom reminded me to bring an umbrella.
My mom reminded me to take an umbrella.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: What does the word in bold mean?
unitTestQuestions.context: After three weeks of negotiation, the talks between the airline and the pilots ended in **deadlock**.
options: a situation where no progress is possible
a successful agreement
a secret deal
a written contract
unitTestQuestions.explanation: **Deadlock** = a situation in which neither side will change its position, so no progress is possible (kebuntuan).
